result.topic_en: Euler eliminates the inclination ρ and the small quantity c to obtain a direct equation for the Moon's distance x from the node, using the observed beginning and end of a lunar eclipse and the immersion and emersion. He then begins to find the moment of true opposition of Sun and Moon.
result.transcription:
De loco lunae ex eclipsibus lunaribus determinando. 373

Ex hac autem formula vicissim ipsa distantia $x$ ita definiri poterit, ut angulus $\rho$ plane non ingrediatur, quatenus particula minima $c$ ab eo pendet. Cum enim sit simili modo
$$\sin^2\tfrac{1}{2}\rho = \frac{\cos(A-B+c)-\cos F}{\cos(A-B+c)-\cos(2x-A-B-c)}$$
erit $$\frac{\cos(A-B+c)-\cos(2x-A-B-c)}{\cos(A-B+c)-\cos F} = \frac{\cos(a-b+c)-\cos(2x-a-b-c)}{\cos(a-b+c)-\cos f}.$$
Ex hac autem aequatione difficilius valor ipsius $x$ eruitur, unde methodo ante tradita potius uti conveniet.

§. 21. Qui autem laborem suscipere velit, atque ex aequationibus successive angulum $\rho$ et particulam $c$ eliminare, is tandem sequentem reperiet aequationem
$$\mathrm{tang}\,2x = \frac{(\cos F-\cos(A-B))(\cos f-\cos(a+b))\sin(A+B)\sin(a-b)-(\cos f-\cos(a-b))(\cos F-\cos(A+B))\sin(a+b)\sin(A-B)}{(\cos f-\cos(a-b))(\cos F+\cos(A+B))\sin(a+b)\sin(A-B)-(\cos F-\cos(A-B))(\cos f+\cos(a+b))\sin(A+B)\sin(a-b)}.$$
Inventa autem distantia $x$ erit porro
$$c = \frac{(\cos f-\cos(a-b))\sin(a+b)\sin 2x}{\cos f\sin(a-b)+\sin 2b\cos 2x-\cos f\sin(a+b)\cos 2x}$$
et $$\mathrm{tang}^2\tfrac{1}{2}\rho = \frac{\cos(a-b)-\cos f-c\sin(a-b)}{\cos f-\cos(a+b)\cos 2x+c\sin(a+b)\cos 2x-\sin(a+b)\sin 2x-c\cos(a+b)\sin 2x}$$
seu $$\mathrm{tang}^2\tfrac{1}{2}\rho = \frac{\cos(a-b)-c\sin(a-b)-\cos f}{\cos f-\cos(2x-a-b)-c\sin(2x-a-b)}.$$
Sicque ex observationibus initii et finis eclipsis, itemque immersionis et emersionis in eclipsi totali, tam locus nodi quam inclinatio orbitae lunae ad eclipticam definiri poterunt. Interim tamen verendum est, ne istae formulae complicatae, ob minimos etiam errores in observationibus commissos, nimium a veritate seducant, ac fortasse saepe tutius erit formulis ante inventis uti.

§. 22. Non difficile hinc erit momentum quoque verae oppositionis solis ac lunae assignare, quo scilicet longitudo centri lunae congruat cum longitudine umbrae. Accidat enim vera oppositio $z$ horis post medium eclipsis momentum; et cum in medio eclipsis esset longitudo centri umbrae a nodo
$$☊\sigma = x \quad\text{et}\quad ☊\lambda = x - \frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\rho}{g(n-m)},$$
erit momento verae oppositionis longitudo centri umbrae a nodo $= x + z(m+k)''$ et distantia lunae a nodo
$$= x + z(n+k)'' - \frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\rho}{g(n-m)}.$$
Sit brevitatis gratia
$$c = \frac{(m+n+2k)\sin 2x\,\mathrm{tang}^2\frac{1}{2}\rho}{g(n+m)}\text{[?]},$$
erit ex conditione verae oppositionis
$$\cos\rho = \frac{\mathrm{tang}(x+z(m+k)'')}{\mathrm{tang}(x-c+z(n+k)'')} = \frac{(\mathrm{tang}\,x+\mathrm{tang}\,z(m+k)'') : (1-\mathrm{tang}\,x\,\mathrm{tang}\,z(m+k)'')}{(\mathrm{tang}\,x+\mathrm{tang}(z(n+k)''-c)) : (1-\mathrm{tang}\,x\,\mathrm{tang}(z(n+k)''-c))}.$$

items.quote: Ex hac autem formula vicissim ipsa distantia $x$ ita definiri poterit, ut angulus $\rho$ plane non ingrediatur, quatenus particula minima $c$ ab eo pendet.
items.english: Conversely, from this formula the distance x itself can be determined in such a way that the angle ρ does not enter at all, insofar as the very small quantity c depends on it.

items.quote: Ex hac autem aequatione difficilius valor ipsius $x$ eruitur, unde methodo ante tradita potius uti conveniet.
items.english: But from this equation the value of x is extracted with more difficulty, so it will be better to use the method given before.

items.quote: Qui autem laborem suscipere velit, atque ex aequationibus successive angulum $\rho$ et particulam $c$ eliminare, is tandem sequentem reperiet aequationem
items.english: Whoever is willing to undertake the labour of successively eliminating the angle ρ and the quantity c from the equations will finally find the following equation.

items.quote: Sicque ex observationibus initii et finis eclipsis, itemque immersionis et emersionis in eclipsi totali, tam locus nodi quam inclinatio orbitae lunae ad eclipticam definiri poterunt.
items.english: Thus from observations of the beginning and end of the eclipse, and likewise of the immersion and emersion in a total eclipse, both the place of the node and the inclination of the lunar orbit to the ecliptic can be determined.

items.quote: Interim tamen verendum est, ne istae formulae complicatae, ob minimos etiam errores in observationibus commissos, nimium a veritate seducant, ac fortasse saepe tutius erit formulis ante inventis uti.
items.english: Meanwhile it is to be feared that these complicated formulas, because of even very small errors committed in the observations, may lead too far from the truth; it will perhaps often be safer to use the formulas found earlier.

items.quote: Non difficile hinc erit momentum quoque verae oppositionis solis ac lunae assignare, quo scilicet longitudo centri lunae congruat cum longitudine umbrae.
items.english: From this it will not be difficult also to assign the moment of the true opposition of the Sun and Moon, namely when the longitude of the Moon's centre coincides with the longitude of the shadow.
